assumptions: The material is the original v12 text (round 1) or the spec copy (later rounds); cross-part references outside the targets may be named under missing_inputs.
obligations.criterion: Supported when every Control rule has a matching model behaviour (or a stated reason it is not modelled) and no path is found by which permitted writes make a not-acceptable artifact accepted or published. Violated when a concrete inconsistency or such a path is shown, with locators.
evidence_requirements: model run output or attack script result
obligations.question: Control layer and reference model: are the control rules of the Control part consistent with the reference model (Appendix A), and can the main Agent, using only the writes the Control part allows (contracts, facts by the permitted writers, admission requests, publish), cause an artifact that should not be accepted to be accepted or published?

missing_inputs: Delivery part (Delivery §2.3 attested definition, §3.1 adapter mapping for ambiguous submissions / cancel semantics), referenced by Control §4.1 and §3
Methods §2.4 (post-hoc correction and multiple-testing rules for confirmation), referenced by Control §4.4 item 4
answers.reasoning: Close reading of Control §0-§8 and the relevant Core sections, a rule-by-rule trace into the reference model, a full model run (90/90 scenarios pass, 42/42 mutations killed, exit 0) and an attack script (work/asg-1/attack.py). Most rules map one-to-one onto model functions: closed format -> validate_contract; strictness order -> step_at_least_as_strict / contract_at_least_as_strict; effective contract, approval position and lapse -> _contracts; execution state -> _exec; producer, owning step and usable -> producers / owner_step / best_producer; currency and upstream state -> self_current / upstream_state; overtaken and binding -> overtaken / bound; checks -> checks_state / valid_check_attempt / check_inputs_hold; freeze -> freeze_ok / independent_sample; admission -> admit; publish -> publish. Two paths were found that let permitted writes (contract, admission/cancel requests, publish) produce a published result that the design says must not be obtained without a human or without trace. (1) The overtaken rule only sees output digests of attempts whose terminal fact is a confirmed receipt/reconcile, so a draw that ends unknown (output seen out of band), or is abandoned and later reconciled with a recorded digest, does not overtake the older artifact. Reverting the step's content then rebinds the older output without a pin, and publish succeeds. The abandoned-and-reconciled case also contradicts the spec text ('any attempt ..., whatever its end state'). (2) A check attempt that ends without a result (cancelled, failed, or timed out after its outcome was visible) leaves no trace in the publish counts or the report: it is not a failed draw, not a confirmation result and not a fail. Admission does not restrict a re-check either. So a confirmation can be retried on fresh samples, or a non-deterministic check redrawn, until it passes, while publish reports confirmation_results=1 and failed_draws=0. One minor wording inconsistency in the state diagram was also found.

findings.claim: The overtaken rule, which is meant to stop the main Agent from choosing among outputs already seen, can be bypassed by a draw that does not end in a confirmed terminal fact. If a newer draw ends unknown, its output is never recorded, because a receipt's output digest is valid only when termination is confirmed. If the draw is abandoned and later reconciled, its digest is recorded but ignored, because the model counts only effective terminal facts and an abandoned attempt has none. In both cases a later revert of the step's content makes the older checked artifact current again, and it binds and is published without the human pin the spec requires. The abandoned-and-reconciled case contradicts Control §4.2 directly: Overtaken covers outputs of 'any attempt of that step name ... whatever its end state'. The unknown case is a spec gap: overtaken is defined over outputs seen in the fact log, but an unknown attempt's output can be seen outside it (the Agent controls the program, so for example a detached child process makes termination unconfirmed).
findings.element: Control §4.2 Overtaken/Binding vs. model candidates_raw/overtaken; Control §2 receipt output digest only when termination is confirmed; Control §3 abandoned outputs
findings.evidence_text: attack.py A1: publish(D) -> X1 while a3 is unknown, label X1 = ok. A2: after abandon + reconcile(outputs=Y), 'Y in candidates_raw: False', overtaken(X1) = False, publish(D) -> X1. Control run with a confirmed Y gives label X1 = overtaken. Fix direction: treat any non-reuse attempt of the step admitted after a's first appearance that has no usable, current output (including unknown, abandoned and abandoned-reconciled) as overtaking a, and index reconcile digests of abandoned attempts.

findings.claim: A check attempt that ends without a result (cancelled, failed in execution, or timed out, for example after its outcome was visible) is invisible in the deliverable status and in publish. failed_draws and the task-wide history count only computation attempts of contract steps. confirmation_results counts only results. Admission places no same-identity restriction on check attempts once one has terminated. So the 'rerunning cannot wash a failure away' guarantee (Control §0 principle 7) and the 'every draw visible' guarantee (Control §4.5, §5.1 item 6) do not hold for checks. A confirmation can be tried on S1, aborted, tried on S2, aborted, and passed on S3, then published as T3C with confirmation_results=1 and failed_draws=0. A non-deterministic required check (toys, resampling) can likewise be redrawn until it passes. The spent samples appear only as raw exposures; they are not in the publish record. Control §4.4 item 3 even names this case ('ended without a result ... the sample is spent') but counts it nowhere.
findings.element: Control §4.5 failed draws / confirmation-sample results (computation attempts only); Control §5.1 item 6 (no rule for check attempts); model failed_draws / task_history / admit __check__ branch
findings.evidence_text: attack.py B1: achieved T3C, publish {prior_failures: 0, failed_draws: 0, confirmation_results: 1} after two aborted confirmation check attempts on S1 and S2. B2: a cancelled check attempt followed by a same-identity re-check that passes is published with failed_draws 0. Model lines 1053-1067 and 1089-1099 iterate over contract step names only (never '__check__'); admit 1237-1246 has no rerun rule for checks.

findings.claim: The state diagram gives cancelling -> failed only for 'receipt failure', but the model (TERMINAL) and every other branch of the diagram also map a confirmed timeout to failed. The diagram omits the timeout transition from cancelling.
findings.evidence_text: Control line 134 'cancelling --> failed: receipt failure, termination confirmed' vs lines 125/129/138 ('failure or timeout') and model TERMINAL line 594 applied in all of admitted/running/cancelling (lines 613-617).
